Ruichang platform SBC uses existing shares held by the platform, so no SBC dilution; count held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 bank interest income 918 + investment income 1,449 (wealth-management products / structured deposits) from the other-income note (FY2025 AR line ~5981). Both stripped from the flows because the deposits and FVTPL portfolio that earn them are added in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back RMB527m (Ruichang platform scheme); EquityAwardTaxes 0 (no net-share settlement). FY2024's RMB2,016m included a one-off RMB1,663m Ruichang platform charge.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases (FY2024-H1 2026 financing activities). The flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company funds; SBC is small (~0.2% of revenue) so the point is immaterial.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB million; H shares quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1744 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-23 21:51Z). Cross-rate check: USD/HKD 7.8413 / USD/CNY 6.6606 = 1.1773, a 0.25% tie, confirming direction (1 CNY = 1.17 HKD). No A-share or ADR dual listing exists for a price parity check. All per-share values computed in CNY and multiplied by fx_rate; unsuffixed intrinsic values are HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.9% + beta 1.2 (cyclical auto OEM, export/tariff exposed) x 6.5% China ERP = ~9.7%; essentially no net financial debt, so WACC ~ cost of equity; 9.5% used. Same 9.5% in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and price-war risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS-16 EBITDA excludes lease cost, lease liabilities RMB4,664m (698 current + 3,966 non-current, 30 June 2026) are in total_debt, principal (RMB291m H1 2026) is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU renewal sits inside the capex % path. lease_cost_pct_path is 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at ~9x run-rate NCI profit (FY2025 RMB488m, H1 2026 RMB449m; ~RMB700m/yr used) = RMB6,300m. Book NCI of RMB609m understates the economic stake, so market-style value is used rather than book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (CNY flows / HKD quote, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule). Chery is an operating passenger-vehicle manufacturer (ICE + NEV, five brands, China's largest exporter), so it routes to the 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' row of dcf-methods/SKILL.md. No MEMORY.md entry exists - first valuation. HORIZON 10 years (FY2026-FY2035), FY0 = FY2025 actuals; the latest balance sheet is 30 June 2026, so half of year-1 FCF already sits in that cash - deducted in the bridge. EBITDA BASIS: the reported 'EBITDA' (operating income + D&A, RMB29,519m FY2025) includes JV/associate share (1,579), bank interest (918), investment income (1,449), FX gains (2,710), a one-off distribution-network disposal gain (1,051) and FV gains (318); stripping those leaves core EBITDA ~RMB21.5bn = 7.2% of revenue FY2025 (H1 2025 ~6.9%, H2 2025 ~7.4%). H1 2026 core is ~9.9% (gross margin 13.0% -> 16.1% on export mix; reported 10.2% after a RMB2,092m FX loss). Recurring PRC subsidies (VAT super-deduction, R&D and other subsidies, ~RMB2.5bn = 0.85% of revenue) are kept in EBITDA. The margin paths are CORE (ex-non-operating) margins and must not be compared to the reported EBITDA margin. CAPEX % includes PP&E, intangible purchases and development spend capitalised through OCF (FY2025 14,654 = 4.9%; FY2024 8,925 = 3.3%; H1 2026 4,547 = 3.2%). WORKING CAPITAL: Chery runs deeply negative operating working capital (payables 145.7bn + other payables 35.8bn + contract liabilities 19.8bn vs inventories 47.8bn + receivables 40.8bn + prepayments 15.5bn at 30 June 2026), so the cash pile is largely supplier float - see the equity_bridge float deductions. Base wc_capture is 0 (no further stretching assumed under the June-2025 60-day supplier-payment pledge; export growth carries longer inventory/receivable cycles); bear uses +10% so that falling volume UNWINDS float (cash out on revenue decline). Reported FCF is dominated by working-capital swings (FY2024 37.3bn, FY2025 5.5bn, H1 2026 35.3bn) and is not a usable base by itself; the component build is the base.

H1-2026 interim line ~1189. Current FVOCI (1,754, bills receivable) is operating working capital and excluded.

equity_bridge.item: Supplier float: H1 2026 bills-payable spike treated as timing
equity_bridge.note: Bills payable rose 19.4bn -> 50.3bn and total trade+bills payables +35.5bn in six months on revenue +1.2%, while restricted deposits fell 10.9bn; the cash/time-deposit build of ~23bn was funded by it and is expected to reverse as the bills mature (<1 year). Interim note 11.

Trade payables 95.3bn ~ 145 days of annualised H1-2026 COGS (240bn). Compliance with the June-2025 OEM 60-day supplier-payment pledge would release ~56bn of float; ~25-30% probability of enforcement on this horizon -> ~15bn expected outflow.

equity_bridge.item: H1 2026 cash flow already in the 30 June balance sheet (half of year-1 owner FCF)
equity_bridge.note: Year 1 is full-year FY2026 but the bridge uses the 30 June 2026 balance sheet; removes the overlap. Offsets roughly against discounting year 1 a full period from October.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue path CAGR (FY2025-FY2035); no historical CAGR is usable as a forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total equity CAGR (82%, FY2022 8.4bn -> FY2025 50.8bn, inflated by the Sept-2025 HK$9.1bn IPO and retained earnings off a tiny base) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (48%) and net income (50%) CAGRs, and all three are hyper-growth off a FY2022 base that does not repeat (FY2026 H1 revenue +1.2%). EPS has only two annual points (2.58 -> 3.43). Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest and investment income) fell from 33.2bn to 2.6bn on a working-capital reversal, so no FCF CAGR is meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: Annual history starts FY2022 (prospectus years); FY2022-FY2023 carry revenue/net income only. Reported FCF swings by 30bn+ a year on supplier-payables timing, so growth is anchored on revenue and margin components, not on FCF.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3%: H1 +1.2% (Q1 -3.4%), H2 helped by export momentum (overseas revenue +51% in H1) against a flat-to-down domestic market. Mid-single-digit growth FY2027-29 as Omoda/Jaecoo and NEV exports compound (1m-unit 2027 brand target only partly delivered), fading to 2.5% as export share matures.
base.margin_rationale: Core EBITDA ex non-operating items: 6.9% H1 2025, 7.4% H2 2025, ~9.9% H1 2026. FY2026 9.0% assumes H2 gives back part of the H1 gain (price war, R&D +28%). Fades to 8.5% - between the FY2025 core and H1 2026 - as the NEV mix (8.8% GM vs 15.0% ICE in FY2025) keeps rising and EU tariffs bite.
base.capex_rationale: 4.3% vs 3.2-4.9% history (incl. capitalised development) while overseas plants (Spain JV, 3 overseas bases) are built, easing to 3.5%; D&A rises from 1.9% (FY2025 1.5%, H1 2026 annualised 2.0%) toward 3.0% so terminal capex/D&A ~1.17x supports 2% growth.
base.tax_rationale: 20% cash rate: FY2025 cash tax paid 5,030 on PBT 23,001 (21.9%, incl. tax on non-operating income); ETR 15.2% FY2025 / 19.8% H1 2026 (HNTE 15% parent, higher overseas rates rising with export mix).
base.terminal_note: Cap 10x terminal FCF (cyclical auto OEM; Chinese OEMs trade at ~5-8x earnings). Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% = 13.6x, so the cap binds.

bull.rationale: Exports keep compounding (Europe, LatAm, Middle East; Spain JV localises around EU tariffs), Omoda/Jaecoo reaches ~1m units, NEV margins close toward ICE, H1-2026 core margin (~10%) holds and edges up with premium mix (EXEED/LUXEED); growth again releases float. Higher capex for overseas capacity.

bear.rationale: Export peak: China's export-permit regime, EU tariff escalation, Russia/Turkey demand or sanctions shocks and Chinese rivals' overseas price war cut overseas volumes from FY2027; domestic share keeps slipping to BYD/Geely. Core margin falls back below the FY2025 7.2% to 5.5% as NEV mix rises at low margin. Falling volume unwinds supplier float (+10% capture on a revenue decline is a cash outflow).

scenario_narratives.base: Chery's export machine keeps growing but the domestic market stays a price war. Revenue +3% in FY2026 (H1 +1.2%) and mid-single digits through FY2029 as overseas sales (now ~70% of revenue on a run-rate basis) and NEVs (41% of revenue) offset domestic ICE decline, fading to 2.5%. Core EBITDA margin gives back part of the H1-2026 jump (16.1% gross margin) and settles at 8.5%, above FY2025's 7.2% core on export mix but held down by rising low-margin NEV share and EU tariffs. Capex runs above D&A while overseas plants are built. The cash pile is credited only after deducting the H1-2026 bills-payable spike and an expected-value charge for 60-day supplier-payment normalisation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chery becomes a scaled global OEM: Omoda/Jaecoo approaches the 1m-unit 2027 target, the Spain JV and other overseas bases localise production around EU tariffs, NEV gross margins converge toward ICE, and premium brands (EXEED, LUXEED) lift mix. Revenue compounds ~6-11% through FY2029, core EBITDA margin rises to 10.5% and growth releases further supplier float. Optionality from a US/Canada/Mexico entry is not modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: Exports peak. The China export-permit regime, higher EU tariffs, a Russia/Turkey demand or sanctions shock and Chinese rivals carrying the domestic price war overseas cut overseas volumes from FY2027 while domestic share keeps slipping (~4.6% NEV retail share vs BYD ~23%). Revenue falls 6% and 4% in FY2027-28 then grows 2%; core EBITDA margin drops to 5.5% as the NEV mix rises at low margin; falling volume unwinds supplier float. This is the path the market's ~6x P/E is pricing.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% default): the thesis rests on export growth into tariff- and sanctions-exposed markets, the domestic price war is unresolved, and Chinese OEM margins have a record of compressing after peaks. Base 50%: H1-2026 margin gains are real but partly mix and timing. Bull 20%: requires several independent things (export compounding, NEV margin convergence, tariff workarounds) to go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Chery is valued as a cyclical, export-led auto OEM on owner FCF built from core (ex-non-operating) margins, with the balance sheet credited for its liquid assets and JV stakes only after deducting the parts of the cash pile that are supplier float rather than owner cash. The headline debate is not the DCF of the car business but how much of RMB~116bn of liquid assets belongs to shareholders: Chery funds itself with ~RMB146bn of trade and bills payables, and that float rose RMB35bn in six months.
key_risks_to_valuation: Supplier-float reversal: the bridge deducts 45bn for the bills-payable spike and expected 60-day normalisation; full normalisation plus the spike would be ~86bn, ~RMB7/share more.
Export concentration and trade policy: EU tariffs (35.3% + 10%), China export permits, Russia/Turkey exposure - the bear axis.
Domestic price war and NEV mix dilution compressing the core EBITDA margin back below 7%.
Margin basis: reported EBITDA includes ~RMB8bn/yr of non-operating income and FX; the paths are core margins, so the H1-2026 jump may be partly mix/timing.
Pre-IPO lock-up expiry (~US$8bn reported overhang) - price, not value, but it may keep the discount open.
Recurring PRC subsidies (~0.85% of revenue) kept in EBITDA could be withdrawn.
